links.outcome: Share of questions answered at a fixed 5% error rate when the model defers the rest
links.effect: At a 5% error rate, RadKev-27B could answer 90.5% of questions versus 76.4% for Kev-27B, so it defers less often at the same error rate.
links.quote: At an error rate of 5%, RadKev-27B could answer 90.5% of questions and Kev-27B 76.4%.

unlisted_practices: Domain-specific fine-tuning of open-weight decision models on public radiology datasets
Running an open-weight model within the hospital so patient data stay local
Categorical decision models that return answer probabilities in one step without generating text, compared with reasoning LLMs on latency

screen.reason: The paper develops and benchmarks fine-tuned open-weight decision models (RadKev) against LLMs and other decision models on held-out radiology tasks (report reading, error detection, diagnosis classification) across automated benchmarks, without testing a clinical deployment practice or safeguard.
